The 2027 Alliance Valor 4310 Debuts as a Fifth-Wheel Toy Hauler That Really Feels Like Home
20 photos
Photo: YouTube/Markhams on the Move
Utility doesn't exclude comfort or aesthetics, though that often seems to be the case with utility-focused fifth-wheel toy haulers. This one wants to be the exception, and while still in prototype stage, you can't but admit that it makes a compelling argument.
This is the Alliance Valor 4310, which is being presented as a 2027 model year but is in reality still just a prototype. It's a fully functional one, though, and it's actually being put through its paces by the couple posting RV content under the Markhams on the Move handle.
The rig was not developed with or built for the Markhams, though they did take delivery of it after Alliance debuted at a recent dealer event, where it was brought out to gauge potential interest in it. As you must know, many big RV companies got in on the deal with rising RV content creators, designing one-off custom units in a sort of partnership agreement, with the view of launching a production floorplan if there was enough interest in that custom unit.
This isn't one of them, but similarities exist. The Markhams say that they already owned a 2023 Alliance that they were looking to upgrade and that they'd been looking specifically into the new Valor 4213 floorplan. They toured that one but did not love it, so they asked for the 4310, of which they'd heard on the grapevine.
Photo: YouTube/The RV Hunter The moment they saw it, they knew it was "the one." At the time they shot the first video below, they'd lived in it for one week and had it set up, but were yet to travel in it, which they planned to do soon. The rig will serve as their permanent home, and the first thing they loved about it was how residential it felt.
It seems that this residential quality was the main focus from the start, as Hunter from The RV Hunter also points out. The Valor 4310 is a fifth-wheel toy hauler that feels like an actual home, where most toy haulers feel like toy haulers with a house attached.
This being a prototype, exact dimensions are still pending, but you're looking at a big and heavy rig , sat on a 101-inch (256-cm) widebody chassis and a triple axle with H-rated Continental tires and upgraded MORryde CRE3000 suspension. It will come standard with an upgraded Curt Helux pinbox, six-point hydraulic auto-leveling, three exterior awnings, and three flush-floor slide-outs, one of which is a super-slide.
Photo: YouTube/The RV Hunter You're also looking at a nice toy hauler with a 14-foot (4.2-meter) garage with a rear patio, complete with a Thule awning, safety railing and gate, and all the necessary tie-downs for your gear. At the same time, though, this garage brings extra functionality, whether you need a mobile office space, an extra bedroom with sleeping for as many as five or six people, or additional storage.
Unlike other garages onboard toy haulers, this one comes with a full dry bathroom, which means that the extra functionality as a bedroom isn't just an afterthought, as well as insulated floors, TV and entertainment, and a separate entrance.
Then, there's the "livability" of the rest of the space . Thanks to the widebody chassis and the smart design, the rest of the rig is a proper home, complete with an island kitchen with a standalone dinette, a generously sized living room with a massive sectional that is equal parts chillout-perfect and a spare bed for two, and a king bedroom with a walk-in wardrobe, heaps of storage, and a pass-through bathroom.
Photo: YouTube/The RV Hunter Styling is residential, too. This toy hauler offers solid surface counters, residential appliances, and solid wood furniture, as well as prep for an optional washer and dryer (in the bedroom space) and all the storage space an entire family might need, regardless of how much time they plan to be spending on the road.
The little comforts of residential life are included. You get a coffee hutch with subway tile backsplash off the kitchen, an island with a massive, all-accessory stainless steel sink, a dedicated pantry with sensor lights, and plenty of space to move around. You get a dinette that will be as comfortable for game nights as it will be for hosting dinner parties.
Features highlighted by Alliance and/or obvious in the video tour below include atrium tinted windows in the living room space and the dinette, extra tall slide-outs, JBL two-zone audio, a TV on a televator in the living room so you can still enjoy the view when you're not tuning in on your favorite movies and shows, Furrion Chill Cube ACs, and a sectional sofa in the living with everything from accent lighting to hidden cup holders and reclining functions.
Photo: YouTube/The RV Hunter Also standard is a full-time RV-ing warranty, Tufflex roof with a telescopic ladder for access, a molded front cap, separate compartments for lithium batteries and a backup generator, a dedicated metal box for tools and other items, and an auxiliary fuel tank for the garage – assuming you will want to actually haul toys in this rig.
As of this writing, the Alliance Valor 4310 is in prototype phase, but the floorplan will debut as a standalone luxury fifth wheel floorplan for the 2027 model year. When that happens, the full list of specs will be made public, but don't let its absence stop you from taking it it visually.
Via // The RV Hunter on YouTube
